function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Below is a quick‑start guide to the most popular “startup‑stat” APIs you can tap into. I’ve grouped them by data focus (funding, valuation, metrics, news, etc.), listed the key endpoints, and shown a minimal Python example (using the built‑in `requests_get` helper) so you can hit the API straight away. > **TL;DR** – If you’re looking for a *single* API that gives you everything (funding, valuation, employee count, news, etc.) you’ll need to stitch together a few services. The table below shows the best fit for each data type. | # | Service | What it gives you | Key endpoint(s) | Free tier? | Notes | |---|---------|-------------------|-----------------|------------|-------| | 1 | **Crunchbase** | Funding rounds, valuations, exits, company profiles, investors | `/v3.1/organizations/{org_id}`
`/v3.1/organizations?name={name}` | Yes (limited calls) | Requires API key; generous free tier for small projects. | | 2 | **AngelList** | Company data, job listings, funding, investors | `/api/v1/companies?name={name}` | Yes (public data) | Uses OAuth2; rate‑limited. | | 3 | **PitchBook** | Detailed financials, valuations, M&A, private equity | `/v1/companies/{id}` | No (paid) | Enterprise‑grade; pricey. | | 4 | **CB Insights** | Funding, valuations, market trends, competitive landscape | `/api/v1/companies/{id}` | No (paid) | Enterprise‑grade. | | 5 | **StartupRank** | Startup rankings, metrics, growth scores | `/api/v1/startups?search={query}` | Yes (limited) | Open‑source project; community‑maintained. | | 6 | **Data.gov US** | Publicly funded startup data (e.g., SBIR awards) | `/api/v1/sbir?state={state}` | Yes | U.S. only. | | 7 | **OpenCorporates** | Company registration, directors, filings | `/v0.4/companies/{jurisdiction_code}/{company_number}` | Yes | Good for legal data. | | 8 | **News APIs** (e.g., NewsAPI.org) | Startup news, press releases | `/v2/everything?q=startup` | Yes (limited) | Good for sentiment analysis. | --- ## 1. Crunchbase – The “go‑to” for funding & valuation Crunchbase offers the most comprehensive public data on private companies. The API is RESTful and JSON‑based. ```python # Example: Search for a company by name response = functions.requests_get({ "url": "https://api.crunchbase.com/v3.1/organizations", "headers": {"Accept": "application/json"}, "params": { "user_key": "YOUR_CRUNCHBASE_API_KEY", "name": "Stripe" } }) print(response) ``` **Typical payload** (simplified): ```json { "data": { "items": [ { "name": "Stripe", "homepage_url": "https://stripe.com", "founded_on": "2010-09-14", "raised_amount_usd": 1100000000, "valuation_usd": 95000000000, "investors": [...] } ] } } ``` > **Tip:** Use the `organization_id` to drill down into funding rounds, exits, and investor details. --- ## 2. AngelList – Quick public data & job listings AngelList’s API is a bit older but still useful for quick lookups. ```python response = functions.requests_get({ "url": "https://api.angel.co/1/companies", "headers": {"Accept": "application/json"}, "params": { "access_token": "YOUR_ANGELLIST_TOKEN", "name": "Airbnb" } }) print(response) ``` > **Note:** The API uses OAuth2; you’ll need to register an app to get a token. --- ## 3. StartupRank – Community‑driven ranking If you want a quick “score” for a startup (growth, traction, etc.), StartupRank is a lightweight option. ```python response = functions.requests_get({ "url": "https://api.startuprank.com/v1/startups", "params": {"search": "Robinhood"} }) print(response) ``` The response includes a `score`, `rank`, and key metrics like `funding`, `employees`, `growth_rate`. --- ## 4. Combining APIs – A quick “starter kit” Below is a tiny script that pulls a company’s basic profile from Crunchbase, then enriches it with a news headline from NewsAPI.org. ```python import json # 1️⃣ Crunchbase lookup crunchbase_resp = functions.requests_get({ "url": "https://api.crunchbase.com/v3.1/organizations", "params": { "user_key": "YOUR_CRUNCHBASE_KEY", "name": "Notion" } }) company = crunchbase_resp["data"]["items"][0] # 2️⃣ NewsAPI search news_resp = functions.requests_get({ "url": "https://newsapi.org/v2/everything", "params": { "apiKey": "YOUR_NEWSAPI_KEY", "q": "Notion", "sortBy": "publishedAt", "pageSize": 3 } }) headlines = [article["title"] for article in news_resp["articles"]] # 3️⃣ Combine result = { "name": company["name"], "valuation": company.get("valuation_usd"), "funding": company.get("raised_amount_usd"), "headlines": headlines } print(json.dumps(result, indent=2)) ``` --- ## 5. Authentication & Rate Limits | Service | Auth | Rate limit (per minute) | Notes | |---------|------|--------------------------|-------| | Crunchbase | API key in query | 60 | Free tier: 1000 calls/day | | AngelList | OAuth2 | 60 | Public data only | | PitchBook | OAuth2 | 30 | Enterprise | | CB Insights | OAuth2 | 30 | Enterprise | | StartupRank | None | 60 | Community | | NewsAPI | API key | 500 | Free tier: 500 requests/day | > **Tip:** Cache responses aggressively (e.g., Redis or local disk) to stay within limits. --- ## 6. Where to get API keys | Service | How to sign up | |---------|----------------| | Crunchbase | https://data.crunchbase.com/signup | | AngelList | https://angel.co/applications | | PitchBook | Contact sales | | CB Insights | Contact sales | | StartupRank | https://github.com/startuprank/startuprank-api | | NewsAPI | https://newsapi.org/register | --- ## 7. Common pitfalls | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | “Invalid API key” | Double‑check the key and that you’re using the correct header/query param. | | “Rate limit exceeded” | Implement exponential backoff or queue requests. | | “Missing fields” | Some companies have incomplete data; always guard against `None`. | | “Data freshness” | Crunchbase updates every 24 h; AngelList may lag. | --- ### Bottom line There isn’t a single “startup stat API” that covers everything, but the combination of Crunchbase (funding & valuation), AngelList (public company data), StartupRank (growth score), and a news API gives you a solid foundation. Pick the ones that match your data needs, keep an eye on rate limits, and you’ll be able to build a robust startup analytics pipeline in minutes. Happy hacking!
